class.name: PlayerInput
class.brief_description: Per-player action state, so two people at one machine can hold different actions.
class.description: Owned by a [LocalPlayer] and fed raw events by the [InputRouter]. Godot's [Input] singleton merges every device into one state, which is why two players cannot share it; this class keeps a separate state per player, filtered by the device slots that player owns. There are two modes, and the difference matters. While [member device_slots] contains [constant DEVICE_SLOT_ALL] the object is in [i]passthrough[/i]: every query is forwarded straight to [Input], so a project that never assigns device slots behaves exactly as it did before per-player input existed. Give the player a specific slot and it switches to tracking its own state. [b]Actions are shared.[/b] There is one [InputMap] for the whole project; this only tracks which of its actions [i]this player's[/i] devices are holding. You do not duplicate actions per player. [b]There is no frame flush.[/b] [method is_action_just_pressed] compares a stamped frame number against the current one, the same way [Input] does, so the answer is correct no matter how many listeners ask or in what order their [code]_process[/code] runs, and it works from [code]_physics_process[/code] too.

method.name: action_press
method.description: Synthetic input, the per-player counterpart of [method Input.action_press]. A filtered player does not see the [Input] singleton, so a game that drives actions from script - or a test, or a remapping UI - has to press them here instead.

method.name: device_slot_from_event
method.description: The device slot an event belongs to: the joypad index for [InputEventJoypadButton] and [InputEventJoypadMotion], otherwise [constant DEVICE_SLOT_KEYBOARD_MOUSE]. Classification is by event class, not by [member InputEvent.device]. Keyboard and mouse have reserved ids ([constant InputEvent.DEVICE_ID_KEYBOARD] and [constant InputEvent.DEVICE_ID_MOUSE]), but a synthesized [InputEventAction] reports [code]0[/code], which would collide with joypad 0.

method.name: feed_input_event
method.description: Called by the [InputRouter]. Does nothing in passthrough, where the engine already holds the state.

method.name: get_action_raw_strength
method.description: The strength before the action's deadzone is applied. Read straight off the joypad axis rather than reconstructed, so it is exact.

method.name: get_vector
method.description: Same contract as [method Input.get_vector], including the circular deadzone. A negative [param deadzone] averages the four actions' own deadzones.

method.name: is_action_just_pressed
method.description: True for exactly one frame after the press. A tap that lands and lifts within one frame reports both this and [method is_action_just_released], matching [Input].

method.name: refresh_action_cache
method.description: The [InputMap] action list is snapshotted. Call this after adding or removing actions at runtime.

method.name: remove_device_slot
method.description: Drops only what that device was contributing, so letting go of the pad does not clear an action the keyboard is still holding.

method.name: reset_action_states
method.description: Releases everything that is held, firing [method is_action_just_released] for it. Called when a pad is unplugged, so no button can stay stuck down with nothing left to release it. Worth calling yourself when the window loses focus.

members.member: The devices that feed this player. A player may own several - keyboard and mouse [i]and[/i] a pad is the normal setup for player 1 in a co-op game.

constants.constant: No device assigned yet. The player exists but is waiting for a press-to-join.
Every device feeds this player. The default for player 0, and what makes a single player project behave exactly as before.
Keyboard and mouse counted as one device. Joypads use their own index, from [code]0[/code] upwards.
